slides.title: Inspectable SQL, with measured limits
slides.subtitle: What the agent does, how well it did, and what to keep in mind
slides.problem: People need answers from databases without writing SQL, but a fluent answer can still be wrong.
slides.approach: An agent picks the relevant tables, writes SQL that runs read-only, and shows it with the rows.

findings.headline: Read-only holds: 45 of 45
findings.text: Safety tests passed on 3 database engines, none skipped.

findings.headline: 64.6 % on Spider, 35.2 % on BIRD
findings.text: Answers matched on a local 9B model, with this project's scorer, not leaderboard scoring.

findings.headline: +3.6 points on large databases
findings.text: Sending the top 6 tables beat every table with hints [+1.4, +5.8], with a 69 % smaller prompt.

findings.headline: Smaller prompts were not faster
findings.text: Each answer took about 2 s longer, because the local model could not reuse its cache.

slides.takeaway: About one answer in three still did not match on Spider, so a person should review results.

notes.purpose: Give the whole story before the detail.
script: Here is the whole story before the detail. [Point: 45 of 45] Read-only comes first: generated SQL is validated and run read-only, and all 45 tests passed on three database engines with none skipped.
[Point: 64.6 % and 35.2 %] With a local 9B model, 64.6 % of Spider dev answers and 35.2 % of the harder BIRD dev answers matched, using this project's scorer. These are not leaderboard scores.

[Point: +3.6 points] On databases of 21 to 65 tables, sending the top six tables and their neighbours scored 3.6 points above sending every table with hints, using 69 % fewer prompt tokens. The gain comes from the 65- and 34-table databases.

[Point: not faster] Those smaller prompts took about two seconds longer per answer, because each question gets a different schema and the local model cannot reuse its cache. [Point: takeaway] About one in three Spider answers still did not match, so a person should review results.
Reference: README Evaluation Results, release runs of 10 October 2026 at 7708295; bird_train_large at 47284f5, 19 October 2026. AGENTS.md 4 November 2026: conformance 45 passed, 0 skipped.

slides.title: A fluent answer can still be the wrong answer
slides.subtitle: Text-to-SQL turns a question into SQL over a schema, then returns rows; each step can go wrong

figure.title: Published scores fall on enterprise tasks
figure.caption: **Source:** share of tasks solved by an o1-preview agent, as reported in the Spider 2.0 paper (2024); not this project's results.

causes.title: Meaning
causes.text: Words like “revenue” are not columns. Gross or net? The schema does not say.

causes.title: Scale
causes.text: Real schemas are large. Spider 2.0 databases often exceed 1,000 columns.

causes.title: Risk
causes.text: Generated SQL runs on real data, so it must be stopped from changing it.

slides.takeaway: Published scores fall about 70 points on enterprise tasks, so a good demo is not evidence.

annotations.title: SQL is the easy part
annotations.text: The hard part is knowing what the question means in this database.

annotations.title: We see the same direction
annotations.text: Spider 2.0 sits 69.9 points below Spider 1.0. Our model also falls on the harder test, from 64.6 % on Spider to 35.2 % on BIRD, using our own scorer.

annotations.title: Keep a person in the loop
annotations.text: A valid query can still answer the wrong question. Dashboards and analyst SQL remain best for defined, recurring metrics.

notes.purpose: Say why a fluent answer is not enough.
script: Text-to-SQL turns a question into SQL over a schema and returns rows. Writing the SQL is the easy part. [Point: Meaning] The hard part is what the question means here. A word like revenue is not a column. [Point: Scale] Real schemas are also large: Spider 2.0 databases often exceed 1,000 columns.

[Point: Spider 2.0 bar] In the Spider 2.0 paper, an o1-preview agent solved 21.3 % of enterprise tasks, against 91.2 % on Spider 1.0 and 73.0 % on BIRD. Our local model also falls on the harder test, from 64.6 % to 35.2 %, on our own scorer.
[Point: Risk] The SQL runs on real data, so it must be stopped from changing that data, and a valid query can still answer the wrong question.
Reference: Spider 2.0 paper, arXiv 2411.07763, read 6 November 2026. 91.2 minus 21.3 is 69.9 points. Project scores: README Evaluation Results.
